paragraphs.source_en:
degree, — the King] Nbk 9; degree, the king 1820, 1839.
 wise: — but man:] Nbk 9; wise: but man 1820, 1839.
 S. is thinking of such things as sexual jealousy, the moral ostracism of ‘fallen women’ and vene-
real disease; cp. lines 153–63 above, and see especially Q Mab viii 129–30, 230–1, ix 76–92.
 Passionless? no —] Nbk 9; Passionless; no, 1820, 1839; S. added the question mark in Leigh Hunt’s
presentation copy of 1820.
 made,] Nbk 9; made 1820, 1839.
 This line is written on the facing page in Nbk 9, replacing S.’s original Which clog that spirit, else
which might outsoar canc. clogs] I.e. impediments.
 Heaven,] Heaven Nbk 9; heaven, 1820, 1839.
 inane] From Lat. inane, ‘Void space’; the word in this sense is frequent in Lucretius, and see
also e.g. Virgil, Eclogue vi 31. After this line in Nbk 9, and at the very foot of the page, S. has written
Prometheus, centred as if to indicate a further speech.
